o: During every time unit covered by at least one interval, enough bulbs must be on that at least `brightness` positions are illuminated; a bulb lights its own cell and its neighbors (up to 3 cells). Energy is (bulbs on) summed over active time, so we need the fewest bulbs per active time multiplied by the total number of active time units. One bulb covers at most 3 positions, so at least ceil(brightness/3) bulbs are needed, and placing them at positions 1, 4, 7, ... achieves full coverage whenever brightness <= n (boundary clipping never forces more, since brightness <= n lets us hug the line). Example 1: ceil(5/3) = 2 bulbs for 7 time units -> 14. Active time is the size of the union of intervals, computed by sorting and merging (coordinates reach 1e9, so per-time-unit simulation is infeasible).
k: Minimum bulbs per active time unit is ceil(brightness / 3): each bulb lights at most 3 cells, and spacing bulbs at 1, 4, 7, ... attains it.
Energy = ceil(brightness/3) * (number of time units covered by the union of intervals).
Interval endpoints reach 1e9, so merge intervals instead of simulating time steps.

a.i: Mark every covered time unit in a boolean array and multiply the count by the per-time bulb requirement. Perfectly clear, but memory/time scale with the largest endpoint (up to 1e9), so it only works on small inputs.
s: Allocate a boolean array up to max endpoint; mark all units inside each interval.
Return need times the number of marked units.
a.t: O(T + sum of interval lengths) where T is the max endpoint — up to 1e9, infeasible at full constraints

a.i: Sort intervals and merge overlapping/adjacent-touching ones; the union size is the sum of merged lengths. Multiply by ceil(brightness/3), the proven-minimum bulb count per active unit.
s: Sort intervals by start; sweep merging overlapping intervals and accumulating each merged block's length (end - start + 1).
a.t: O(m log m) for sorting plus O(m) merge sweep, m = number of intervals

w: Prove the ceil(brightness/3) bound both ways in the interview: information-theoretic lower bound (each bulb covers <= 3 cells) and the explicit placement at 1, 4, 7, .... Pitfalls: double-counting overlapping intervals (must merge, see example 3), 64-bit products (1e5 intervals x 1e9 length overflows int), and off-by-one on inclusive endpoints. Follow-ups: different brightness per interval, or bulbs that consume different energy.
